featured.title: Oil Nears $100 as Middle East Conflict Deepens
featured.content: Global energy markets are under renewed pressure after Iran-aligned Houthi forces attacked targets in Saudi Arabia while the wider U.S.-Iran conflict continued to threaten regional energy infrastructure and shipping routes. Brent crude climbed to around $99.49 a barrel on Wednesday, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate reached about $94.63. Saudi authorities said Houthi attacks injured 73 people and caused fires and temporary operational disruptions at some energy facilities. The developments are increasing concerns about prolonged supply disruption, higher transport costs and renewed inflationary pressure worldwide.
featured.imageQuery: Brent crude oil refinery energy market Middle East

articles.title: Middle East Conflict Pushes Oil Towards $100
articles.content: Oil prices climbed for a fourth consecutive session on Wednesday as attacks involving Iran-aligned Houthis, Saudi Arabia, the United States and Iran increased fears of further disruption to global energy supplies. Brent rose to around $99.49 a barrel while WTI reached about $94.63.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Reports 73 Injured in Houthi Attacks
articles.content: Saudi authorities said attacks by Iran-aligned Houthi forces hit several southern Saudi cities and energy facilities. Fires were reported and some operations were temporarily halted while emergency teams responded. Saudi authorities said 73 people were injured.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia oil refinery energy facility

articles.title: Global Markets Turn Cautious as Oil Approaches $100
articles.content: Asian markets were mixed on Wednesday as investors weighed rising geopolitical risks against stronger technology shares. Japan's Nikkei rose about 0.6%, South Korea's KOSPI gained around 1.6% and Taiwan's TAIEX added about 0.6%, while several other regional markets weakened. Investors are also watching upcoming U.S. inflation data.

articles.title: U.S.-Iran Escalation Keeps Markets on Edge
articles.content: The United States and Iran remain locked in an escalating confrontation, with U.S. action against Iranian oil tankers and an Iranian missile attack on a U.S. base in Jordan adding to fears of a wider regional conflict. The developments have pushed energy markets sharply higher.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran conflict map military Middle East

articles.title: Bank of England Expected to Keep Rates at 3.75%
articles.content: A Reuters poll of 65 economists found that the Bank of England is expected to leave its Bank Rate at 3.75% through the remainder of 2026. Higher energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict have complicated the outlook for inflation and future rate cuts.

articles.title: Dangote Warns Global Fuel Shortages Could Last Beyond Iran Conflict
articles.content: Dangote Refinery says global fuel shortages could persist even after the current Iran conflict because of damage to refining infrastructure, high refinery utilisation and the need to rebuild depleted fuel inventories. The refinery reported a $1.82bn profit in the first half of 2026, compared with a $476m loss a year earlier.

articles.title: Dangote Plans $14.3bn Refinery Expansion
articles.content: Dangote plans to invest about $14.3bn to expand its refining capacity from around 700,000 barrels per day towards 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029. The company is also preparing an IPO expected to raise about ₦2.15tn, or roughly $1.63bn, with the offer scheduled to run from September 14 to October 13.

articles.title: Nigeria Oil-Theft Incident Leaves at Least 37 Reportedly Dead
articles.content: At least 37 people are reported to have died after inhaling toxic fumes during an attempted crude-oil theft operation in Rivers State. The Nigerian police confirmed that an incident occurred and said investigations were continuing, but no official death toll has been released. RadiantWaves therefore reports the figure as 'at least 37 reportedly dead' rather than as an officially confirmed toll.

articles.title: South African Economy Contracts in Second Quarter
articles.content: South Africa's economy contracted 0.2% quarter-on-quarter in the second quarter of 2026, according to official statistics. The contraction was linked to weaker domestic demand and poor performance in sectors including mining and manufacturing, while higher energy prices have added another external pressure.
articles.imageQuery: Johannesburg South Africa business district economy

articles.title: Gambia Protests Erupt Over Prolonged Power Cuts
articles.content: Protests broke out in several parts of The Gambia after residents experienced electricity outages lasting up to 48 hours in some areas. Demonstrators burned tyres and erected barricades, while police used tear gas. President Adama Barrow acknowledged the hardship and promised additional generators and a new 24MW generation unit, alongside plans for a 50MW solar project.
articles.imageQuery: Gambia Banjul protest electricity power outage

articles.title: Burundians Seek to Leave Kenya Amid Immigration Anxiety
articles.content: Hundreds of Burundians gathered at their embassy in Nairobi seeking travel documents to return home, amid concerns about Kenya's new measures affecting undocumented foreign traders. Kenya has announced a temporary 90-day amnesty for undocumented East Africans to regularise their status. Kenyan officials say the policy is intended to enforce documentation and business regulations rather than target foreigners.

articles.title: DR Congo Tightens Control Over Strategic Geological Data
articles.content: The Democratic Republic of Congo is expanding state control over geological information used in mining exploration. The country is accelerating mapping, airborne surveys and digitisation of geological archives covering major deposits of cobalt, copper, lithium and gold. Officials say better geological information could reduce exploration risks while strengthening Congo's negotiating position with investors.
articles.imageQuery: DR Congo cobalt copper mining geological survey

articles.title: Yen Holds Near Seven-Month High
articles.content: The Japanese yen strengthened towards a seven-month high against the U.S. dollar as traders increased expectations that the Bank of Japan could raise interest rates. The currency was around 153.66 per dollar on Wednesday, after reaching about 152.89 during the previous session.
articles.imageQuery: Japanese yen currency Tokyo financial district

articles.title: Global Diesel Supplies Expected to Remain Tight Through Winter
articles.content: Industry executives warn that global diesel supplies could remain tight through the winter as refining capacity is constrained by geopolitical disruptions, maintenance delays and high seasonal demand. The pressure is being felt even though crude supply itself remains more resilient than supplies of refined products.

articles.title: AI and Semiconductor Stocks Provide Support for Asian Markets
articles.content: Technology and semiconductor shares offered some support to Asian markets despite broader concerns over oil prices and geopolitical risk. Investors remain focused on the impact of higher energy costs on inflation and interest-rate decisions.

morningSummary.title: 🌍 RadiantWaves Morning News & Update
morningSummary.content: Good morning. Global markets are beginning Wednesday under pressure as oil approaches $100 a barrel amid escalating Middle East tensions. In Africa, Nigeria's Dangote Refinery is preparing a major expansion while warning that fuel shortages could remain tight. South Africa's economy contracted in the second quarter, protests have erupted in The Gambia over electricity shortages, and Kenya's immigration regularisation measures have created anxiety among some foreign traders. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen remains strong and investors are watching inflation data and central-bank decisions closely.

bigQuestion: With oil prices approaching $100 and geopolitical tensions spreading across regions, are African countries sufficiently prepared to protect their economies from another global energy shock?
